Build an observed-data resampling specification

Source: R/api-resampling.R
build_mfrm_resampling_spec.Rd

Build an observed-data resampling specification

Usage

build_mfrm_resampling_spec(
  data,
  person,
  facets,
  score,
  strata = NULL,
  preserve_facets = NULL,
  design = c("stratified_subsample", "stratified_bootstrap"),
  reps = 20,
  sample_fraction = 0.5,
  sample_n = NULL,
  replace = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  min_per_stratum = 1,
  topup_preserve_facets = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A long-format observed MFRM data set with distinct column names. The .mfrm_* metadata columns listed below are reserved and must not already be present. Numeric identifiers must retain distinct text labels.

person

Person/respondent identifier column.

facets

Non-person facet columns used by the target MFRM fit.

score

Ordered score column.

strata

Optional person-level stratification columns, for example a Region or L1 group column. Each person must have at most one unique stratum combination.

preserve_facets

Optional facet columns whose level coverage should be reviewed and, when possible, topped up after the stratified person draw. A common choice is the rater facet.

design

Resampling design. "stratified_subsample" samples persons without replacement inside each stratum. "stratified_bootstrap" samples persons with replacement inside each stratum and re-keys duplicate person instances in the returned data.

reps

Number of resampling replicates to draw.

sample_fraction

Fraction of persons to draw within each stratum when sample_n = NULL. Targets are rounded upward and respect min_per_stratum. The default is 0.5 for both designs; use 1 for a same-size bootstrap.

sample_n

Optional target number of persons to draw per stratum. Supply either one scalar used for every stratum, or a named numeric vector whose names match spec$target_plan$Stratum. An unnamed vector of length equal to the number of strata follows that table's order. Targets are rounded upward and capped at available Persons when sampling without replacement.

replace

Optional logical override for replacement. By default, replacement is FALSE for "stratified_subsample" and TRUE for "stratified_bootstrap".

seed

Optional seed used by draw_mfrm_resamples().

min_per_stratum

Minimum target persons per represented stratum.

topup_preserve_facets

Logical; if TRUE, add extra person clusters when possible to recover missing levels of preserve_facets. This changes the sampling distribution and can increase stratum sizes; it is not an ordinary bootstrap. Set FALSE for ordinary cluster-bootstrap draws.

Value

An object of class mfrm_resampling_spec containing the input data, columns, target plan, person/stratum rosters, sampling_scheme and interpretation in terminology.

Details

This helper defines a resampling design for observed-data stability checks. It is intentionally separate from build_mfrm_sim_spec() and simulate_mfrm_recovery(). The full-data estimates used with these draws are reference estimates, not known truth, so downstream summaries should be described as estimation stability, reproducibility, or agreement with a full-data reference rather than strict parameter recovery.

The design is person-clustered: all rows for a selected person are kept together. For bootstrap draws, duplicated person clusters are re-keyed in the returned data while the original identifier is retained in .mfrm_original_person.

Sampling assumptions and interpretation

For ordinary stratified Person-cluster bootstrap draws, set design = "stratified_bootstrap", sample_fraction = 1, sample_n = NULL, and topup_preserve_facets = FALSE. The unit is a Person, not a rating row; unequal-sized clusters retain all their rows on every draw. This targets variation across independent Persons within strata, conditional on the observed non-Person facet levels and assignment patterns. It does not reproduce sampling new raters or tasks, or dependence across Persons induced by shared random effects or peer-review networks. Crossed random effects require a resampling scheme matched to that sampling target.

A reduced sample size or coverage top-up instead defines a stability experiment. Top-up chooses an additional Person carrying a currently absent preserved level, and can also bring other missing levels. It changes inclusion probabilities and stratum totals. Use sampling_scheme, the returned terminology and base/added/final counts to report what was drawn. These helpers do not fit models or construct confidence intervals; the presence of the word bootstrap does not qualify downstream interval coverage. Reference estimates from the full sample still have estimation uncertainty.

Labels and saved specifications

Original Person keys and data values are retained. Stratum labels escape percent signs and vertical bars, and distinguish missing values, empty strings and literal "(missing)"/"(empty)" labels. Inspect target_plan before supplying named sample_n values. Data column names .mfrm_original_person, .mfrm_draw_unit, .mfrm_stratum, .mfrm_topup, and .mfrm_topup_reason are reserved for returned metadata.

draw_mfrm_resamples() rebuilds derived tables from the specification's declared inputs, including saved older specifications. Corrected labels and top-up rules can change old draws even with the same seed; retain old results separately. saveRDS(spec, ...) preserves the input data and seed; saveRDS(draws, ...) preserves the actual samples, per-replicate seeds and manifests. Use an explicit seed to reproduce draws in a matching R/RNG environment. Manifest-only results retain the specification and input data but omit the materialized samples.

References

Owen, A. B. and Eckles, D. (2012). Bootstrapping data arrays of arbitrary order. The Annals of Applied Statistics, 6(3), 895–927. doi:10.1214/12-AOAS547 . This discusses crossed-factor resampling; it is not the method implemented by this Person-cluster helper.

See also

draw_mfrm_resamples(), build_mfrm_sim_spec()

Examples

# Bundled synthetic ratings: inspect stability in half-samples by Group.
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")
spec <- build_mfrm_resampling_spec(
  ratings, person = "Person", facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score", strata = "Group", preserve_facets = "Rater",
  reps = 2, sample_fraction = 0.5, seed = 99
)
draws <- draw_mfrm_resamples(spec)
summary(draws)$overview
#>                 Design                                 SamplingScheme Reps
#> 1 stratified_subsample coverage_augmented_stratified_person_subsample    2
#>   SamplesReturned Replace PreserveCoverageCompleteRate TopupReps
#> 1               2   FALSE                            1         0
#>   GapOrFallbackReps
#> 1                 0
draws$stratum_manifest  # Base, top-up and final Person-cluster counts.
#>     ResampleID Replicate Stratum AvailablePersons TargetPersons
#> 1 resample_001         1       A               24            12
#> 2 resample_001         1       B               24            12
#> 3 resample_002         2       A               24            12
#> 4 resample_002         2       B               24            12
#>   BasePersonClusters Rows TargetStatus SelectedPersonClusters
#> 1                 12   70           ok                     12
#> 2                 12   70           ok                     12
#> 3                 12   71           ok                     12
#> 4                 12   71           ok                     12
#>   SelectedOriginalPersons TopupPersonClusters
#> 1                      12                   0
#> 2                      12                   0
#> 3                      12                   0
#> 4                      12                   0
